note: Hand-written study wording: what the sign means and what you actually do. Kept apart from signs.json so rebuilding the catalogue never overwrites it. Not the legal text - the wording of the executive order always wins.

meanings.A11: A junction ahead where the side road must give way to you. You keep priority, but slow enough to react if someone pulls out.
meanings.A16: A roundabout is coming. Traffic already in the roundabout has priority, so plan your lane and speed before you arrive.
meanings.A17: A pedestrian crossing ahead. Be ready to stop; people on the crossing always go first.
meanings.A18: The road ahead carries traffic in both directions again, often after a one-way stretch or roadworks. Keep right and expect oncoming cars.
meanings.A19: Traffic signals ahead, often where you cannot see them from far. Ease off the accelerator so a sudden red does not surprise you.
meanings.A20: Queues form here. Look far ahead, brake early and use your hazard lights if you have to stop sharply.
meanings.A21: Cyclists cross or join the road here. Check your right side and your blind spot before turning.
meanings.A22: Children may be on or near the road - school, playground, sports ground. Drop your speed and expect the unexpected.
meanings.A23: Riders on horseback use this road. Pass slowly and widely, and avoid revving or sounding the horn.
meanings.A26: Wild animals cross here, most often at dawn and dusk. If one appears, brake in a straight line rather than swerving.
meanings.A27: Farm animals may be on the road. Slow right down and be ready to stop until they are well past.
meanings.A31: The road can be slippery. Increase your distance, brake gently and avoid sudden steering.
meanings.A33: Loose chippings can be thrown up by tyres. Slow down and leave a bigger gap so you do not stone the car in front.
meanings.A34: Falling rocks. Watch the road surface for debris and do not stop under the slope.
meanings.A35: The shoulder is soft or drops away. Keep away from the edge, especially when meeting a wide vehicle.
meanings.A36: A speed bump ahead. Slow down before it, not on it.
meanings.A36.1: An actibump: the road surface dips if you arrive too fast. Keep to the limit and nothing happens.
meanings.A37: The surface is uneven - holes, ruts or frost damage. Reduce speed to keep control.
meanings.A38: A dip in the road. You lose sight of what is beyond it, so ease off before you reach it.
meanings.A39: Roadworks ahead. Expect narrow lanes, workers on the road and temporary yellow markings, which override the ordinary white ones.
meanings.A41.1: A sharp curve to the right. Brake before the bend, not in it.
meanings.A41.2: A sharp curve to the left. Brake before the bend and keep well right so you do not cut into oncoming traffic.
meanings.A42.1: Several bends, the first to the right. Set a speed you can hold through the whole sequence.
meanings.A42.2: Several bends, the first to the left. Set a speed you can hold through the whole sequence.
meanings.A43.1: The road narrows from both sides. Adjust speed and position early, and be ready to give way if there is no room for two.
meanings.A43.2: The road narrows from the left. Keep an eye on traffic merging towards you.
meanings.A43.3: The road narrows from the right. Keep an eye on traffic merging towards you.
meanings.A44: A tunnel ahead. Switch on your dipped headlights, take off sunglasses and keep your distance.
meanings.A46.2: A steep uphill gradient. Change down in good time and expect slow heavy vehicles.
meanings.A72: A level crossing without gates. Approach slowly, look both ways and never start crossing unless you can clear it completely.
meanings.A73: A level crossing with gates. Stop when the lights or barriers say so, and never zigzag around a closing barrier.
meanings.A74.1: A single-track level crossing is right here.
meanings.A74.2: A multi-track level crossing is right here - one train can hide another.
meanings.A75: Countdown markers to a level crossing: the crossing is close, take your foot off the accelerator.
meanings.A91: An opening bridge ahead. It can stop traffic completely, so watch for signals and queues.
meanings.A92: A quayside or riverbank without a barrier. Keep your speed low and your distance from the edge.
meanings.A95: Strong side winds, typically on bridges and open stretches. Hold the wheel firmly and expect a shove when you leave shelter.
meanings.A96: Low-flying aircraft can appear suddenly and loudly. Do not let it distract you from the road.
meanings.A97: Low-flying helicopters, often near a hospital or airfield. Keep your attention on the road.
meanings.A99: A danger that has no sign of its own. The subpanel underneath tells you what it is - read it.
meanings.B11: Yield. Give way to traffic on the crossing road; you may roll on without stopping only if it is genuinely clear.
meanings.B13: Stop. You must come to a complete standstill at the line, even on an empty road, and only then give way.
meanings.B15: Lanes merge ahead. Merge in turn, one car from each lane, at a speed that fits the other line.
meanings.B16: You are on a main road: traffic from side roads gives way to you. Priority does not mean you stop looking.
meanings.B17: The main road ends here. From now on the ordinary give-way rules apply, including priority to the right where nothing says otherwise.
meanings.B18: Oncoming traffic has priority in the narrow stretch ahead. Wait on your side until it is clear.
meanings.B19: You have priority over oncoming traffic in the narrow stretch ahead, but do not force your way through if someone is already in it.
meanings.C11.1: No right turn at this junction.
meanings.C11.2: No left turn at this junction.
meanings.C12: No U-turns here. Find a junction or a place where turning is allowed.
meanings.C19: No entry: the road ahead is one-way against you. If you see this sign, you are about to drive into oncoming traffic.
meanings.C21: Traffic is prohibited in both directions - the road is closed to you, whichever way you are going.
meanings.C22.1: No motor vehicles. Bicycles, pedestrians and horse riders may still use the road.
meanings.C23.1: No heavy goods vehicles above the weight the sign or its subpanel states.
meanings.C25.2: No small mopeds. Bicycles are still allowed.
meanings.C26.1: No riding or leading a horse.
meanings.C31: Maximum permitted total weight of the vehicle, in tonnes as shown. If your vehicle is heavier, take another route.
meanings.C32: Maximum permitted weight of a vehicle with trailer, in tonnes as shown.
meanings.C35: Maximum axle load in tonnes as shown.
meanings.C36: Maximum bogie load in tonnes as shown.
meanings.C41: Maximum width, load included. Mirrors and overhanging loads count.
meanings.C42: Maximum height, load included. Measure before you meet a bridge you cannot pass under.
meanings.C43: Maximum length of the vehicle, or of the whole combination with a trailer.
meanings.C51: No overtaking from here until the restriction ends. It applies to overtaking motor vehicles, not to bicycles and mopeds.
meanings.C52: Heavy goods vehicles may not overtake from here.
meanings.C54: The restriction on overtaking by heavy goods vehicles ends.
meanings.C55: The local speed limit. It applies from this sign until another limit, an end sign or a change of area cancels it.
meanings.C56: The local speed limit ends. The general limit for the road takes over - 50 km/h in a built-up area, 80 km/h outside it unless signposted otherwise.
meanings.C59: The prohibition shown on the sign ends here.
meanings.C61: No stopping: you may not even pause here, except to obey traffic or to let a passenger get out where that is allowed.
meanings.C62: No parking. Stopping briefly to set down or pick up people or goods is still allowed.
meanings.C92: You may not continue past this point without stopping - typically at customs or a checkpoint.
meanings.D11.1: You must drive in the direction the arrow shows.
meanings.D11.2: You must drive in the direction the arrow shows.
meanings.D11.3: You must drive in the direction the arrow shows.
meanings.D11.4: You must drive in the direction the arrow shows.
meanings.D11.5: You must drive in the direction the arrow shows.
meanings.D11.6: You must drive in one of the directions the arrows show.
meanings.D11.7: You must drive in one of the directions the arrows show.
meanings.D11.8: You must drive in one of the directions the arrows show.
meanings.D12: Drive round the roundabout in the direction of the arrows, and give way to traffic already in it.
meanings.D15.2: You must pass the obstacle on the side the arrow points to.
meanings.D15.3: You must pass the obstacle on the side the arrow points to.
meanings.D16: You may pass the obstacle on either side.
meanings.D21: A cycle track: cyclists and small mopeds must use it, and cars must keep off it.
meanings.D23: A bridleway for horse riders only.
meanings.D26: A path split into separate lanes for cyclists and pedestrians - keep to the side that is yours.
meanings.D26.1: A path split into separate lanes for cyclists and pedestrians - keep to the side that is yours.
meanings.D26.2: A path split into separate lanes for cyclists and pedestrians - keep to the side that is yours.
meanings.D26.3: A path split into separate lanes for cyclists and pedestrians - keep to the side that is yours.
meanings.D26.4: A path split into separate lanes for cyclists and pedestrians - keep to the side that is yours.
meanings.D26.5: A path split into separate lanes for cyclists and pedestrians - keep to the side that is yours.
meanings.D27: A shared path: cyclists and pedestrians use the same surface, so cyclists must take account of people on foot.
meanings.D27.1: A shared path: cyclists and pedestrians use the same surface, so cyclists must take account of people on foot.
meanings.D55: Minimum speed. If your vehicle cannot hold it, you may not use this road.
meanings.E11.1: The lane you are in continues straight on.
meanings.E11.6: From this lane you may go straight on or turn left.
meanings.E11.7: From this lane you may go straight on or turn right.
meanings.E11.8: From this lane you may turn left or right.
meanings.E11.9: From this lane you may go straight on or turn either way.
meanings.E15: How the lanes are arranged at the junction ahead. Pick your lane before you get there.
meanings.E16.1: The number of lanes is reduced ahead. Merge in turn where the lanes meet.
meanings.E16.2: The number of lanes is reduced ahead. Merge in turn where the lanes meet.
meanings.E17: A pedestrian crossing is here. Pedestrians on it have priority, and you may not overtake immediately before it.
meanings.E18: A dead end: the road has no way through, so do not take it as a shortcut.
meanings.E19: A one-way street. Traffic runs only in the direction of the arrow, so do not expect oncoming cars - and never enter from the other end.
meanings.E21.3: A recommended route for horse riders.
meanings.E22.1: A recommended route for heavy goods vehicles.
meanings.E22.2: A recommended route for vehicles carrying dangerous goods.
meanings.E22.3: A recommended route for tractors and slow vehicles.
meanings.E24: Information for people with impaired vision.
meanings.E26.1: A pedestrian bridge over the road.
meanings.E26.2: A pedestrian tunnel under the road.
meanings.E30: A light rail stop. Expect people crossing to and from the platform, and never block the tracks.
meanings.E31: A bus stop. You may not park here, and you must let a bus pull out from the stop in a built-up area.
meanings.E33.1: Parking is allowed here. Any subpanel says who may park, for how long and when.
meanings.E33.2: An indoor or multi-storey car park.
meanings.E34: A breakdown bay for emergencies - not a rest stop.
meanings.E35: A tunnel. Dipped headlights on, keep your distance, and follow the emergency instructions if traffic stops.
meanings.E37: A crawler lane begins for slow vehicles climbing the hill.
meanings.E39: An advisory speed for the stretch ahead. It is not a limit, but it is a good idea when conditions are normal.
meanings.E40: The advisory speed no longer applies.
meanings.E41: A recommended speed for the slip road or ramp.
meanings.E42: A motorway starts here. Motorway rules apply: no pedestrians, cyclists, mopeds or slow vehicles, no U-turns, no reversing.
meanings.E43: An expressway starts here. Similar restrictions to a motorway, but the road may have junctions on the same level.
meanings.E44: The motorway ends. Ordinary road rules and speed limits take over.
meanings.E45: The expressway ends. Ordinary road rules and speed limits take over.
meanings.E47: A bicycle street: cycling sets the pace and cars are guests who must adapt.
meanings.E49: A pedestrian zone. Motor traffic is only allowed where a subpanel says so, and always on pedestrians' terms.
meanings.E51: A living street. Walking pace, children may play on the road, pedestrians have priority, and you may only park in marked spaces.
meanings.E52: The living street ends. Before you rejoin ordinary traffic you must give way to it.
meanings.E53: A traffic-calmed zone: speed humps and narrowings, and a low limit shown on the sign.
meanings.E55: You are entering a built-up area. Unless another limit is signposted, 50 km/h applies from here.
meanings.E56: The built-up area ends. Unless another limit is signposted, the general 80 km/h limit outside towns applies.
meanings.E68: A zone where parking is prohibited on every street until the end sign.
meanings.E68.2: A zone where stopping is prohibited on every street until the end sign.
meanings.E68.3: A parking zone: parking is allowed on the terms shown on the sign.
meanings.E68.4: A zone with a local speed limit that applies on every street inside it.
meanings.E68.5: A zone that heavy goods vehicles may not enter.
meanings.E68.9: A low-emission zone. Only vehicles meeting the emission requirements may drive here.
meanings.E69.5: The zone closed to heavy goods vehicles ends.
meanings.E70: Information about the parking rules that apply in the area.
meanings.E90: Automatic speed enforcement is used on this stretch.
meanings.E91: A sign that shows your speed as you pass. It is feedback, not a fine.
meanings.E92: A variable-message sign: what it shows now is what applies now, and it overrides the fixed signs.
meanings.E93: The area is under video surveillance.
meanings.U1.1: Distance to what the main sign warns about or regulates.
meanings.U1.2: Distance to what the main sign warns about or regulates.
meanings.U2.1: The stretch over which the main sign applies.
meanings.U2.2: The stretch over which the main sign applies.
meanings.U3.1: How long the rule on the main sign applies - here, one hour.
meanings.U3.2: The day of the week on which the main sign applies.
meanings.U3.3: The hours on which the main sign applies. Times in brackets are Saturdays; times in red are Sundays and public holidays.
meanings.U3.4: How long the rule on the main sign applies.
meanings.U3.5: The day of the week on which the main sign applies.
meanings.U3.6: The hours on which the main sign applies.
meanings.U4.1: The vehicle types the main sign applies to.
meanings.U4.2: The vehicle types the main sign applies to.
meanings.U5.1: Bicycles and small mopeds are exempt from the main sign.
meanings.U5.2: Bicycles and small mopeds are exempt from the main sign.
meanings.U6.3: Shows the layout of the junction and where the rule on the main sign applies.
meanings.U6.4: Shows the layout of the junction and where the rule on the main sign applies.
meanings.U7: Cyclists and small mopeds may make the turn the main sign otherwise forbids.
meanings.UA22: The children warned about are on their way to or from school.
meanings.UA31: The road can be icy - typically a bridge, which freezes before the rest of the road.
meanings.UA41: The speed the bend can be taken at in good conditions.
meanings.UA43: The width limit through the narrow stretch.
meanings.UA43.1: A narrow road where you may have to give way to oncoming traffic.
meanings.UA72: Watch out for trains at the crossing ahead.
meanings.UA73: Overhead electric lines at the crossing - dangerous for high vehicles and loads.
meanings.UA99: A junction where accidents happen often. Slow down and look twice.
meanings.UB11.1: A stop sign follows shortly, so start slowing now.
meanings.UB11.2: The cycle track you are about to cross carries traffic in both directions - look both ways.
meanings.UB11.3: A light rail line crosses here.
meanings.UC33: Parking is limited on the terms shown.
meanings.UC56: The restriction applies inside the built-up area.
meanings.UC60.1: The restriction applies both before and after the sign.
meanings.UC60.2: The restriction starts at the sign.
meanings.UC60.3: The restriction ends at the sign.
meanings.UC60.5: Stopping on the shoulder is not allowed.
meanings.UC60.6: Parking on the shoulder is not allowed.
meanings.UC60.7: Parking on the shoulder is allowed.
meanings.UC60.8: Parking partly on the pavement is allowed.
meanings.UC61: Specifies where and when the no-stopping rule applies.
meanings.UC62: Specifies where and when the no-parking rule applies.
meanings.UD1: Points to the lane or path the main sign applies to.
meanings.UD21.1: The cycle track carries cyclists in both directions.
meanings.UE33.1: The parking rule applies before and after the sign.
meanings.UE33.2: The parking rule applies after the sign.
meanings.UE33.3: The parking rule applies before the sign.
meanings.UE33.4: The parking space is for charging electric vehicles.
meanings.UE34: A fire extinguisher and an emergency telephone are here.
meanings.F11: An arrow sign pointing to a destination on the ordinary road network.
meanings.F12: An arrow sign in green: it points along a motorway route.
meanings.F13: An arrow sign in blue: it points along a main road route.
meanings.F14: A temporary arrow sign, used while roadworks or an event change the usual route.
meanings.F16: The exit sign at the junction itself: this is where you leave.
meanings.F18: A stacked list of destinations with the direction of each one.
meanings.F21.1: A numbered cycle route. Follow the number, not the road name.
meanings.F21.2: An arrow sign for cycle and foot paths.
meanings.F21.3: A stacked list of destinations for cycle and foot paths.
meanings.F21.4: A map of the path network ahead, so you can pick your way before the junction.
meanings.F33.2: A stacked list of parking places with their directions.
meanings.F34.1: A signposted diversion route. Follow the whole series of signs, not just the first one.
meanings.F34.2: An arrow sign along a diversion route.
meanings.F34.3: A map of the diversion route ahead.
meanings.G11: A sign on a gantry over the carriageway, telling each lane where it leads.
meanings.G14: A map of the junction ahead, showing which way each road runs.
meanings.G15: A diagram of the lanes ahead and where each of them goes.
meanings.G18: A stacked advance sign: the destinations of the junction ahead, in order.
meanings.H41: Distances in kilometres to the places listed.
meanings.H42: Distances to places in two different directions.
meanings.H45: The name of the place, river, forest or landmark you are passing.
meanings.H46: You are crossing into another region.
meanings.H47: You are crossing into another municipality.
meanings.H49: You are entering a national park.
meanings.H49.1: You are entering a nature park.
meanings.H50: You are leaving the national park.
meanings.H50.1: You are leaving the nature park.
meanings.H51: The national border. Rules, limits and fines change on the other side.
meanings.I11: The exit is here. If this is yours, you should already be in the right lane.
meanings.I12: The exit is 500 metres ahead - time to move over.
meanings.I13: The exit is 1500 metres ahead. The lower panel names the exit after it.
meanings.I16: Here is the exit onto another motorway.
meanings.I17: The exit onto another motorway is 500 metres ahead.
meanings.I18: The exit onto another motorway is 1500 metres ahead.
meanings.I20: A motorway interchange: motorway meets motorway, so choose your lane early.
meanings.J11: Mounted over a lane: this is where that lane takes you.
meanings.J12: Advance warning of how the lanes change ahead.
meanings.J13: A map of the motorway junction ahead.
meanings.K11: Confirmation after a junction: you are on the road you wanted.
meanings.K12: Distances to the places along the road you are on.
meanings.K30: Tourist information: a sight or a service, not a traffic rule.
meanings.M18: A transport hub where you can change between modes of transport.
meanings.M24.1: A charging station for electric vehicles.
